material_definitions: The material investigated is the lithium argyrodite Li6+xP1-xGexS5I, where aliovalent substitution of Ge for P is explored.
Increasing Ge content induces anion site disorder and significantly reduces the activation barrier for ionic motion.
This composition achieves the fastest lithium argyrodite conductivity so far in a cold-pressed state.
The resulting high ionic conductivity allows for successful implementation within a thick-electrode solid-state battery.
The material investigated is the lithium argyrodite Li6+xP1-xGexS5I, where aliovalent substitution of Ge for P is explored.
Increasing Ge content induces anion site disorder and significantly reduces the activation barrier for ionic motion.
This composition achieves the fastest lithium argyrodite conductivity so far upon sintering.
The resulting high ionic conductivity allows for successful implementation within a thick-electrode solid-state battery.

Inspired by the possibility of incorporating Ge into a composition possessing a larger unit cell, the effect of Ge4+ substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I on the structure-transport relationships was investigated.
The study used Rietveld refinements against neutron and X-ray diffraction data to identify structural changes associated with the Li- and anion-substructures, including changes to the site-disorder.
With increasing Ge-fraction, the diffusion pathways for Li+ expand and site disorder between the S2– and I– positions appears.

The increasing disorder is correlated to a sharp decrease in the activation barrier and an increase in the conductivity over orders of magnitude leading to the highest lithium argyrodites reported so far.

In this work, aliovalent substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I was performed and the changes to the structure and transport were investigated.

Using a combination of X-ray and neutron diffraction, nuclear magnetic resonance and impedance spectroscopy, the lattice variations, Ge solubility and, more specifically, the Li+ occupancies and I	extendash/S2	extendash sitedisorder were monitored.
With increasing Ge content, a significant change in the activation barrier was observed, which coincides with an increase of the I	extendash/S2	extendash sitedisorder.
The structural changes and increasing lattice volume lead to an opening of the bottle necks and nuclear magnetic resonance indicates more facile inter-cage jumps.
